checks.name: JENSEN REDUCTION: the bound is concave in A, so the conditional mean suffices
checks.detail: A |-> min(D0, L-a, sqrt(a^2+2A)-a) is a min of concave functions, hence concave. So E[bound(A_sigma) | a,r] <= bound(E[A_sigma | a,r]), and E_omega[A_sigma | a,r] <= n/2 would give the 7.54% margin with NO concentration input -- one conditional-mean inequality in place of concentration of a functional.

checks.name: REFUTED: the natural POINTWISE explanation A_near <= A_far is FALSE
checks.detail: 676 violations out of 3250 opposite-sign edges (20%). If it held, A_near <= (n - D0)/2 < n/2 would follow deterministically -- no Jensen, no probability. Minimal counterexample: lambda = (5, 2, 1) with corners at c = 1 and -2, near = 1, A_near = 4 > A_far = 2 -- the diagram is wide, so the near side carries more area despite the far corner sitting further out. The conditional-mean inequality is therefore a genuine AVERAGING statement with no elementary pointwise route behind it.
